title: NPDev Config v1
$comment: storage/FULL_SUPPORT_PLAN.md W6.1. NOTHING validated this file until 2026-08-08, and the moment something did, 27 corpus configs failed with 93 errors -- including the T1-frozen, shipped npdev-canary. The schema, not the corpus, was mostly wrong: it demanded a `database` block 15 working apps have never had, demanded Postgres connection fields from engines that do not listen on a port, and forbade a `console` section four official apps use and a gate already reads. Widening a schema nobody checks is widening a comment, so the contract was corrected FIRST and the enforcement (check-config-schema.py) added second.

database.description: How the SCENARIO provisions a database for this app. Optional: an app whose engine needs no provisioning (h2-local, in-memory) is complete without it, and 15 corpus apps have always been -- `database` was in `required` until 2026-08-08 only because nothing ever checked. The app's own persistence contract is db.definition.json; this block is the scenario harness's side of it.

allOf.$comment: storage/FULL_SUPPORT_PLAN.md W6.1: the connection fields are required for the engines that LISTEN, and meaningless for the ones that do not. Demanding host/port/username/password from h2-local is what made the shipped canary invalid against its own schema; making them optional for everyone would be the opposite error -- a postgres/mysql/sqlserver scenario with no host is a configuration that cannot work, and it should fail here rather than at connect time.

provider.description: The engine this scenario provisions. Kept in step with DatabaseEngine (NPDevGenerator/.../dbconfig/DatabaseEngine.java) -- an engine selectable there but absent here would be a configuration the platform supports and its own schema rejects, which is what `h2-local` was for as long as this enum said Postgres or nothing.

build.description: deps-and-java/PLAN.md D1/D2: build facts, not domain truth -- kept out of model.json on purpose (a new model.json array triggers the four-place threading hazard that produced REG-108).

javaVersion.description: The generated app's own Gradle toolchain language version. Platform modules (dsl/kernel/generator/adapters/runtimehost source) stay pinned at 17 regardless of this value -- only the generated app's own compile/run toolchain is variable. ROUND2_PLAN.md R1c: no upper enum on purpose -- any integer >=17 is accepted at this layer; the real ceiling (whatever the generated app's own bundled Gradle wrapper/foojay resolver can actually resolve a JDK for) is enforced by Gradle itself at build time, not guessed at here.

repositories.description: deps-and-java/PLAN.md W2.1: extra Maven repositories the app's own build.dependencies[] may need beyond mavenCentral() (always implicitly available).

dependencies.description: deps-and-java/PLAN.md W2.1/D2 (AppDependenciesEmitter, npdev-dependencies.gradle): app-scoped third-party dependencies. String shorthand = implementation + Maven coordinate.

oneOf.description: A local jar, resolved relative to <model.json's own directory>/libs/ at generation time.
A Maven BOM, imported via Gradle's platform(...) so it constrains versions without itself becoming a direct dependency.

databaseMode.description: ADVISORY. Which persistence mode this scenario's notes describe; the app's real engine comes from db.definition.json's database.engine, and no code reads this field. It stays enumerated anyway so a typo is caught (`h2local-file` was one, found the day this schema was first enforced), and it accepts BOTH spellings the corpus uses: the kebab scenario names and DatabaseEngine's own externalName values -- both are canonical somewhere in the platform, and rewriting ten app definitions in a non-repo layer to unify cosmetics would be churn, not correctness.

defaults.description: Behaviour-setting defaults for the whole app, as settingId -> value (NPDev resolution-pipeline envelope).

overrides.description: Per-target setting overrides keyed by selector (module:Name | concept:Name | field:Concept.field).

packs.description: Third-party packs to compose into this app's model. GeneratorMain.readInstalledPackAliases reads `packs.included` on every run -- and this schema forbade the whole section until 2026-08-08, so a user following the documented pack-install path would have written a config the generator accepts and the contract rejects. Found by enforcing the schema for the first time; no corpus app used it yet, which is exactly why it went unnoticed.

console.description: The generated app's admin console posture (scripts/appgen/New-AppConsole.ps1). Four official apps have carried this for months and run-app-upgrade-contract-gate.ps1 already branches on whether an app definition declares it -- so it is real, used, and was rejected by this schema purely because nothing had ever validated a config.json. additionalProperties stays open: this is an AppGen-layer section whose shape is owned by the console generator, and pinning a shape here from a single example is how a schema starts refusing valid input again.
